title: Still Getting Emails After Unsubscribing? What to Do
html:
After you unsubscribe, Gmail says it may take a few days to stop. If mail keeps coming after that, use Manage subscriptions, which unsubscribes you from all active lists from that sender, then report what still arrives as spam. Blocking a sender sends its mail to Spam but does not unsubscribe you.

Last updated: 10 Oct 2026. These are the Gmail app's steps.

Sources last checked: 10 Oct 2026.

Give it a few days

Gmail's help says that after you unsubscribe it may take a few days for you to stop receiving emails from the mailing list. A sender may also have more than one list, and unsubscribing from one email might only remove you from that single mailing list.

Unsubscribe from the whole sender

In the Gmail app on Android, tap Menu at the top left, then Manage subscriptions. Next to the sender, tap Unsubscribe. Google says this unsubscribes you from all active mailing lists related to the sender, and that new emails from them go to your Spam folder. It can take a few days for the sender to process it.

When there is no Unsubscribe link

Some senders only let you unsubscribe on their website, and Gmail shows Go to website instead. If a message has no unsubscribe option at all, treat it as spam: do not click anything in it, and report it. Gmail learns from the spam you report, and reported mail goes to your Spam folder.

Blocking is not unsubscribing

If you block a sender, future mail goes straight to Spam. It does not remove you from their list, so they may keep sending. Blocking is right for senders you never signed up with. For a company you did use, unsubscribe first.

If you never signed up, the cause may be someone using your address by mistake: see getting emails meant for someone else.

If it still does not stop

  • Contact the company through the address on its website or app and ask in writing to be removed. Keep a copy.
  • If the messages look like scams, do not click anything: see how to spot phishing.
  • A flood of mail after a leak is worth checking: has your email been in a breach?

What to do next

  1. Wait a few days after you unsubscribe.
  2. Use Manage subscriptions to remove the sender everywhere.
  3. Report the rest as spam, and block senders you never signed up with.
